cards.q: Define the radian.
cards.a: The angle at the centre of a circle made by an arc equal in length to the radius. A full circle is 2π\displaystyle 2\pi2π radians.

cards.q: Convert 90° into radians.
cards.a: 1.6 rad (π2\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{2}2π​)
steps: 360∘=2π rad\displaystyle 360^\circ = 2\pi\ \text{rad}360∘=2π rad, so multiply degrees by 2π360\displaystyle \frac{2\pi}{360}3602π​.
90×2π360=π2\displaystyle 90 \times \frac{2\pi}{360} = \frac{\pi}{2}90×3602π​=2π​
=1.6 rad\displaystyle = 1.6\ \text{rad}=1.6 rad

cards.q: Define angular speed, and state its unit.
cards.a: The angle turned through per unit time: ω=ΔθΔt\displaystyle \omega = \frac{\Delta\theta}{\Delta t}ω=ΔtΔθ​. Unit: rad s−1\displaystyle \text{rad s}^{-1}rad s−1.

cards.q: Write the equations linking angular speed ω\displaystyle \omegaω to the speed v\displaystyle vv, the frequency f\displaystyle ff and the period T\displaystyle TT of an object moving in a circle of radius r\displaystyle rr.
cards.a: ω=vr=2πf=2πT\displaystyle \omega = \frac{v}{r} = 2\pi f = \frac{2\pi}{T}ω=rv​=2πf=T2π​

cards.q: A wheel turns at 300 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed.
cards.a: 31 rad s−1\displaystyle 31\ \text{rad s}^{-1}31 rad s−1
cards.why: Convert revolutions per minute to revolutions per second first.
steps: Frequency: f=30060=5.0 Hz\displaystyle f = \frac{300}{60} = 5.0\ \text{Hz}f=60300​=5.0 Hz.
ω=2πf=2π×5.0\displaystyle \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 5.0ω=2πf=2π×5.0
ω=31 rad s−1\displaystyle \omega = 31\ \text{rad s}^{-1}ω=31 rad s−1

cards.q: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Explain why it is accelerating.
cards.a: Its velocity is changing, because its direction is changing.
marks: Velocity is a vector: it has direction as well as magnitude.
The direction of motion changes continuously, so the velocity changes.
A change of velocity is an acceleration, directed towards the centre of the circle.

cards.q: Write two expressions for centripetal acceleration.
cards.a: a=v2r=ω2r\displaystyle a = \frac{v^{2}}{r} = \omega^{2}ra=rv2​=ω2r

cards.q: Write two expressions for centripetal force.
cards.a: F=mv2r=mω2r\displaystyle F = \frac{mv^{2}}{r} = m\omega^{2}rF=rmv2​=mω2r
cards.why: It always acts towards the centre of the circle.

cards.q: A student adds "centripetal force" as an extra arrow on the free-body diagram of a car going round a bend. What is wrong?
cards.a: Centripetal force is not a separate force. It is the name for the resultant force towards the centre, which here is provided by friction between the tyres and the road.

cards.q: What provides the centripetal force for a satellite in orbit, a car on a flat bend, and a ball whirled on a string?
cards.a: Satellite: gravity. Car: friction. Ball: the tension in the string.

cards.q: A car of mass 1200 kg travels at 15 m s−1\displaystyle 15\ \text{m s}^{-1}15 m s−1 round a bend of radius 50 m. Calculate the centripetal force needed.
cards.a: 5.4×103 N\displaystyle 5.4 \times 10^{3}\ \text{N}5.4×103 N
steps: F=mv2r=1200×15250\displaystyle F = \frac{mv^{2}}{r} = \frac{1200 \times 15^{2}}{50}F=rmv2​=501200×152​
F=5.4×103 N\displaystyle F = 5.4 \times 10^{3}\ \text{N}F=5.4×103 N

cards.q: The maximum frictional force between a 1200 kg car and the road is 6000 N. Calculate the greatest speed at which it can take a bend of radius 50 m without skidding.
cards.a: 16 m s−1\displaystyle 16\ \text{m s}^{-1}16 m s−1
steps: At the greatest speed, friction just provides the centripetal force: F=mv2r\displaystyle F = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}F=rmv2​.
v=Frm=6000×501200\displaystyle v = \sqrt{\frac{Fr}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{6000 \times 50}{1200}}v=mFr​​=12006000×50​​
v=16 m s−1\displaystyle v = 16\ \text{m s}^{-1}v=16 m s−1

cards.q: How much work does the centripetal force do on an object moving in a circle at constant speed?
cards.a: None. The force is always perpendicular to the direction of motion, so the object's kinetic energy and speed stay constant.

cards.q: A roller-coaster car goes over the top of a vertical loop of radius 4.0 m, upside down. Calculate the minimum speed at the top for it to stay on the track. (g=9.81 m s−2\displaystyle g = 9.81\ \text{m s}^{-2}g=9.81 m s−2)
cards.a: 6.3 m s−1\displaystyle 6.3\ \text{m s}^{-1}6.3 m s−1
cards.why: The mass cancels: the result is the same for any car.
steps: At the top, weight and the contact force both act towards the centre: mg+N=mv2r\displaystyle mg + N = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}mg+N=rmv2​.
At the minimum speed the contact force is zero: mg=mv2r\displaystyle mg = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}mg=rmv2​.
v=gr=9.81×4.0=6.3 m s−1\displaystyle v = \sqrt{gr} = \sqrt{9.81 \times 4.0} = 6.3\ \text{m s}^{-1}v=gr​=9.81×4.0​=6.3 m s−1

cards.q: Use a vector diagram to derive the expression a=v2r\displaystyle a = \frac{v^{2}}{r}a=rv2​ for centripetal acceleration.
cards.a: a=v2r\displaystyle a = \frac{v^{2}}{r}a=rv2​
steps: In a short time Δt\displaystyle \Delta tΔt the object turns through a small angle Δθ\displaystyle \Delta\thetaΔθ, and its velocity vector turns through the same angle.
The velocity vectors before and after, both of length v\displaystyle vv, form a narrow triangle with the change in velocity: Δv=vΔθ\displaystyle \Delta v = v\Delta\thetaΔv=vΔθ.
a=ΔvΔt=vΔθΔt=vω\displaystyle a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = v\frac{\Delta\theta}{\Delta t} = v\omegaa=ΔtΔv​=vΔtΔθ​=vω.
Since ω=vr\displaystyle \omega = \frac{v}{r}ω=rv​, a=v2r\displaystyle a = \frac{v^{2}}{r}a=rv2​. The change in velocity points towards the centre.

cards.q: Define impulse, and state how it relates to momentum.
cards.a: The force multiplied by the time for which it acts. It equals the change in momentum: FΔt=Δp\displaystyle F\Delta t = \Delta pFΔt=Δp.

cards.q: A tennis ball of mass 0.060 kg is hit from rest and leaves the racket at 40 m s−1\displaystyle 40\ \text{m s}^{-1}40 m s−1. The contact lasts 4.0 ms. Calculate the average force on the ball.
cards.a: 600 N
steps: Change in momentum: Δp=0.060×40=2.4 kg m s−1\displaystyle \Delta p = 0.060 \times 40 = 2.4\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}Δp=0.060×40=2.4 kg m s−1.
F=ΔpΔt=2.44.0×10−3\displaystyle F = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \frac{2.4}{4.0 \times 10^{-3}}F=ΔtΔp​=4.0×10−32.4​
F=600 N\displaystyle F = 600\ \text{N}F=600 N

cards.q: Explain why a seat belt that stretches slightly reduces the force on a passenger in a crash.
cards.a: It increases the time taken for the passenger to stop.
marks: The passenger's change in momentum is the same however they are stopped.
The stretching belt increases the time over which the momentum changes.
F=ΔpΔt\displaystyle F = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}F=ΔtΔp​, so a longer time gives a smaller force.

cards.q: How is conservation of momentum applied to a collision in two dimensions?
cards.a: Momentum is a vector, so it is conserved separately in each of two perpendicular directions. Resolve every momentum into components and apply conservation along each direction.

cards.q: A 2.0 kg trolley moving east at 3.0 m s−1\displaystyle 3.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}3.0 m s−1 collides with a 1.0 kg trolley moving north at 6.0 m s−1\displaystyle 6.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}6.0 m s−1. They stick together. Calculate their speed after the collision.
cards.a: 2.8 m s−1\displaystyle 2.8\ \text{m s}^{-1}2.8 m s−1, at 45° north of east.
steps: Momentum east: 2.0×3.0=6.0 kg m s−1\displaystyle 2.0 \times 3.0 = 6.0\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}2.0×3.0=6.0 kg m s−1. Momentum north: 1.0×6.0=6.0 kg m s−1\displaystyle 1.0 \times 6.0 = 6.0\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}1.0×6.0=6.0 kg m s−1.
Each is conserved. Total momentum: 6.02+6.02=8.49 kg m s−1\displaystyle \sqrt{6.0^{2} + 6.0^{2}} = 8.49\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}6.02+6.02​=8.49 kg m s−1.
Combined mass is 3.0 kg: v=8.493.0=2.8 m s−1\displaystyle v = \frac{8.49}{3.0} = 2.8\ \text{m s}^{-1}v=3.08.49​=2.8 m s−1.
The two components are equal, so the direction is 45° north of east.

cards.q: How do you determine whether a collision is elastic or inelastic?
cards.a: Compare the total kinetic energy before and after. If it is the same, the collision is elastic. If some kinetic energy has been transferred to other forms, it is inelastic.
cards.why: Momentum is conserved in both, so momentum cannot tell them apart.

cards.q: Derive the equation Ek=p22m\displaystyle E_{k} = \frac{p^{2}}{2m}Ek​=2mp2​ for the kinetic energy of a non-relativistic particle.
cards.a: Ek=p22m\displaystyle E_{k} = \frac{p^{2}}{2m}Ek​=2mp2​
steps: Start with Ek=12mv2\displaystyle E_{k} = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}Ek​=21​mv2 and p=mv\displaystyle p = mvp=mv.
From the second, v=pm\displaystyle v = \frac{p}{m}v=mp​.
Substitute: Ek=12m(pm)2=p22m\displaystyle E_{k} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{p}{m}\right)^{2} = \frac{p^{2}}{2m}Ek​=21​m(mp​)2=2mp2​.

cards.q: An object of mass 0.50 kg has a momentum of 4.0 kg m s−1\displaystyle 4.0\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}4.0 kg m s−1. Calculate its kinetic energy.
cards.a: 16 J
steps: Ek=p22m=4.022×0.50\displaystyle E_{k} = \frac{p^{2}}{2m} = \frac{4.0^{2}}{2 \times 0.50}Ek​=2mp2​=2×0.504.02​
Ek=16 J\displaystyle E_{k} = 16\ \text{J}Ek​=16 J

cards.q: Outline an experiment to investigate the relationship between the force on an object and its change of momentum.
cards.a: Accelerate a trolley with a known constant force and measure its change of momentum over a measured time.
marks: Pull a trolley along a friction-compensated runway with a string over a pulley to a falling mass, which provides a constant force.
Use two light gates and a timer to measure the trolley's velocity at each gate and the time taken between them.
Calculate the change in momentum: mass × change in velocity.
Repeat for different forces, moving masses from the trolley to the hanger so the total mass stays constant.
Compare force × time with the change in momentum: they should be equal.

cards.q: Outline how video analysis can be used to study a collision between two small spheres on a table top.
cards.a: Film the collision from above and use the frames to find each sphere's velocity before and after.
marks: Film the collision from directly above, with a scale such as a metre rule in the picture.
Use software to mark each sphere's position frame by frame; the time between frames is known.
Find the velocity (speed and direction) of each sphere before and after the collision.
Calculate the momentum of each sphere and resolve it into two perpendicular components.
Check that the total momentum in each direction is the same before and after, and compare the total kinetic energies.
